Author: K. Suresh Reddy
Bench: K. Suresh Reddy
 In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh: Amaravati
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Suresh Reddy
 Criminal Petition No.4605 of 2023
Oral Order

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh: Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
:
The accused in Crime No.103 of 2023 of Pattabhipuram Police Station, Guntur District, filed the present petition under Section 438 Cr.P.C., seeking pre-arrest bail.

2. The above crime was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(1), 307, 323, 506 & 509 I.P.C.
3.
On the basis of the complaint lodged by one Mannepalli Lavanya, the aforesaid crime has been registered.

The contents of the complaint are as follows: The defacto complainant, who is the resident of Patancheru, Sangareddy District, got acquainted with the accused through a common friend by name Unnith Reddy @ Chintu in the year 2021 and since September, 2022, they came into direct contact with each other.

The accused told that he fell in love with her and after two months,
she accepted his love.
The accused used to come to the house of the defacto complainant and she also used to go to his house at Narsingi in Hyderabad.

Subsequently, on coming to know that the accused was making video calls to other girls, the defacto complainant stopped talking to him, upon which the accused tendered apologies and told that he would stop all those things and made her to continue the relationship.

One month thereafter, the defacto complainant came to know that the accused was already married to another woman and when she questioned him, the accused admitted the same and told that they were already divorced and that he wanted to live with the defacto complainant.

Later, on the invitation of the accused to attend his sister's marriage on 23.03.2023,
the defacto complainant went to Guntur on 22.03.2023 and the accused, having booked a room in Annapurna The Royal Hotel for her stay, did not take her to the marriage and made her to stay in the hotel room only.
Therefore, the defacto complainant returned to Hyderabad.
Subsequently, the accused tendered apologies and requested her to come back to Guntur.
On his request, the defacto complainant went to Guntur on 28.03.2023 and the accused arranged a room in the same hotel for her stay and used to meet her in that room every day.

While so, on 31.03.2023 at about 6.00 a.m.,
the accused came to her room, picked up a quarrel with her, abused her in filthy language and beat her with hands and knees on stomach, private parts and also all over her body.
He also tried to kill her by throttling and covered her mouth with his hand and when she bit his hand, he tied her hands with her dupatta and committed rape on her.
When she fell unconscious, he erased the entire data in her mobile phones.

At about 11.00 a.m., she regained consciousness and then the accused tried to take her to his house, but she escaped and went to her friend's house in an auto and her friend CRLP/4605/2023 on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6212064/
1 arranged a room in Hotel Varsha Grand near Guntur Bus stand, for her stay.
On 02.04.2023, after recovering to some extent, the defacto complainant went to the Government Hospital and as per their advice, she lodged the present complaint.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the alleged incident took place on 31.03.2023,
whereas the defacto complainant lodged the complaint on 02.04.2023.
He further contends that all the allegations are false and the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present crime.
Learned counsel further submits that the injuries alleged to have been received by the defacto complainant are superficial in nature.
He, therefore, requests for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
5. On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposes the application.
6. This Court has considered the matter and perused the entire material available on record.

Even according to the own version of the defacto complainant, she used to visit the house of the accused at Hyderabad and even before the alleged incident, she voluntarily went to Guntur and stayed in a hotel room allegedly arranged by the accused.

Considering the circumstances and since prima facie the injuries sustained by the defacto complainant in the alleged incident appear to be superficial in nature, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner with certain conditions.

7. Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender before the Station House Officer,
Pattabhipuram Police Station, Guntur, within a period of two weeks from today and on such surrender, the petitioner shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for Rs.20,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Thousand only) with two sureties for a like sum each to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer, Pattabhipuram Police Station.
After release, the petitioner shall report before the aforesaid Station House Officer once in a week, i.e., on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. and 1.00 p.m., until further orders.
8. This criminal petition is allowed accordingly.

_ _ K. SURESH REDDY, J Dt: 21.07.2023 IBL CRLP/4605/2023 on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6212064/
